newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Steady progress for Guinness H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Steady progress for Guinness H1.

text.p: Guinness Plc's first half results, due on September 26, are expected to show the "steady performance in profit progress" flagged by chairman Tony Greener at the annual meeting in May, analysts said on Friday.
So attention is likely to focus on what the beer and spirits giant might say about its worldwide markets, they added.
"I don't think they are going to tell us anything we don't already know on profits, but we are a bit starved of information on markets," said one analyst who asked not to be named.

Analysts are expecting Guinness to turn in half year pretax profits of 337 to 353 million stg compared with 340 million stg a year ago, with a dividend payout of 4.5 to 4.54 pence per share, up from 4.2 pence.
Around 40 percent of Guinness' year profits fall in the first half as the company's business takes a seasonal boost from Christmas.

Analysts will be looking for any signs that mature markets for spirits such as the U.S., northern Europe and Japan are showing growth along with indications that developing markets are continuing to expand.
"If they say the spirits side is looking stronger, that would be very good news indeed," said Steven Baird, analyst at SG Strauss Turnbull.

Canadian company Seagram raised hopes the spirit sector might be due for a bounce when it announced earlier this month that net profits rose to $62 million for the second quarter, up from $50 million a year earlier.
"Seagram seemed to show things might be picking up and even if Guinness does not say anything, improved results might make the market more bullish," the analyst said.
Guinness' brewing business, meanwhile, is expected to show good progress. One analyst suggested turnover here could top that of spirits for the first time.
Analysts are also likely to look out for the company's marketing budget, after Greener announced its spending plans for the first time last year.

He said at the annual meeting in May that the company would continue to increase the level of marketing investment in both its United Distillers spirits arm and Guinness Brewing Worldwide subsidiaries.
One industry watcher said attention to this could be sharpened as the UK has only recently decided to allow advertising of spirits on television.
As to overall strategy, the company was forced to admit in July that it had no intentions to bid for rival Grand Metropolitan or demerge its brewing business after a leak to the Sunday Telegraph.
"They really had to spell it out. They are just going to soldier on," said the analyst.
